name: Google Digital Wellbeing
purpose: See how you spend time on your phone, set app timers, and build a more intentional bedtime routine.
bestFor: Android students who want a gentle first look at phone habits.
privacy: Built into supported Android devices. Some features vary by manufacturer, version, or account setup.
limitations: Menu names and available features differ across Android devices; app timers can be changed.

name: Apple Screen Time
purpose: Review device use, set app limits, and schedule Downtime across supported Apple devices.
bestFor: Apple students who want usage visibility without adding another app.
privacy: A built-in Apple feature; syncing and reporting behavior depends on your Apple Account and device settings.
limitations: Settings and labels vary by OS version; some features are designed for family or child accounts.

name: Forest
purpose: Turn a focus session into a growing virtual forest so a study block feels visible and motivating.
bestFor: Students who enjoy visual progress and a little gamification while studying.
privacy: Account and sync behavior can vary by platform; review the current store listing and privacy policy.
limitations: Feature availability and pricing vary by platform and region; it is a support tool, not a guarantee of focus.

name: StayFocusd
purpose: Limit or block distracting websites so your browser is better aligned with the task in front of you.
bestFor: Laptop students who lose study time to a predictable list of websites.
privacy: Browser extensions can request broad access. Read the store listing, publisher, and permissions before installing.
limitations: Browser-focused rather than phone-wide; current store availability, permissions, and controls can change.

name: Cold Turkey Blocker
purpose: Block distracting websites and, with supported features, applications during scheduled work blocks.
bestFor: Students who need firmer desktop boundaries than a browser-only extension provides.
privacy: Installation can require elevated permissions for blocking features; review the official requirements and policy.
limitations: Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and iOS are not supported according to the current system requirements page.

name: Android Do Not Disturb
purpose: Silence interruptions, choose exceptions, and schedule calmer study or bedtime windows.
bestFor: Android students who want to reduce notification noise without installing a new app.
privacy: Built into Android. The exact settings and automation options vary by device and Android version.
limitations: Some devices now surface this through Modes; emergency calls, alarms, and exceptions need careful review.

name: Apple Focus
purpose: Create study, personal, or sleep profiles that silence or allow selected people and apps.
bestFor: Apple students who want a repeatable notification routine with scheduled profiles.
privacy: A built-in Apple feature; Share Across Devices and Focus status are configurable settings.
limitations: Available controls and names vary by iOS, iPadOS, or macOS version; exceptions can be easy to overlook.

name: uBlock Origin
purpose: Filter unwanted content and reduce exposure to advertising and tracking requests in supported browsers.
bestFor: Students who want a capable browser-level privacy and content-filtering layer.
privacy: Open-source project; permissions and browser compatibility should be reviewed for the exact extension variant.
limitations: Full uBlock Origin support differs from uBlock Origin Lite; Chrome support and capabilities are changing.

name: Privacy Badger
purpose: Automatically learn and block third-party trackers that follow you across sites without clear consent.
bestFor: Students who want a low-maintenance tracker protection starting point.
privacy: EFF says it does not share browsing data unless you choose to submit a broken-site report.
limitations: Chrome on Android does not support extensions; a site may need a one-site exception if something breaks.

name: Bitwarden
purpose: Generate, store, and use stronger unique passwords across devices instead of reusing one password.
bestFor: Students juggling many accounts who want a repeatable password habit.
privacy: Requires an account and a master password; review the current plan, encryption, recovery, and sync details.
limitations: A password manager cannot recover a forgotten master password for you; account recovery needs planning.
